newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico confirms to make $6 bln prepayment on Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: Mexico confirms to make $6 bln prepayment on Aug 6.

text.p: A source at the Finance Ministry confirmed Monday that Mexico plans to go ahead on Wednesday with a previously-announced prepayment of debt totaling $6 billion.

The debt prepayment, first announced June 17, covers various notes that were issued Aug 5 last year. The prepayment is in line with the government's strategy of aiming to lengthen debt maturites and lower interest rates.
Average annual interest rates of the debt will drop to 7.98 percent from 8.39 percent and average maturities will rise to 6.8 years from 2.6 years, the ministry said when it announced the program.
Funds to prepay the debt have been raised through various recent bond issues, a short-term bank credit and a medium-term notes program, the source said.
